newsitem.title: USA: BP raises 5-year Alaska E&P budget by $1 bln.
newsitem.headline: BP raises 5-year Alaska E&P budget by $1 bln.

text.p: BP Exploration Alaska Inc, a unit of British Petroleum Co Plc, plans to increase its capital spending in Alaska by $1 billion over the next five years, said Alaska Governor Tony Knowles.
The company's yearly outlay will rise from $500 million to an average of $700 million, the governor said in a statement.
Total capital spending will rise to $3.5 billion over the next five years from $2.5 billion.

"We firmly believe Alaska and the oil industry are headed in the right direction and we now have world class opportunities in our sights," said BP Alaska President John Morgan in a joint statement with the governor.
Knowles said the increased investments could add four billion to five billion barrels in recoverable oil reserves over the next decade.
Production of Alaska North Slope crude has declined to about 1.4 million barrels-per-day currently from over two million bpd in 1988.
More than half of all North Slope production projected by the year 2000 depends on investments yet to be made, Knowles said.
BP's increased capital will apply to projects such as the Northstar oil field and enhanced oil recovery efforts at other North Slope fields.
